title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving Health assistance to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach in Dinsor District of Bay Region

description.narrative: ltpgtDinsor Health Response Project is a comprehensive humanitarian health initiative targeting 25,000 vulnerable individuals across seven underserved locations in Dinsoor Health Center, (Holwadag, and Village) Korka Mari IDP, (Section siinay area of Kacanka) Tuur Waluun IDP (Holwadag section October)Waaberi mobile site section Buullo Cadey IDPltbrgtThe project aims to address critical gaps in healthcare access, particularly in areas heavily affected by climate-induced shocks, displacement, and weak health infrastructure. Over a 12-month implementation period, the project will operationalize one fixed primary health care facilities and deploy two mobile health teams/outreach units to ensure equitable, lifesaving healthcare access for both IDPs and host communities.ltbrgtThe intervention is designed to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality through the provision of an essential package of integrated primary healthcare services. These include outpatient consultations, maternal and reproductive health, routine immunization, nutrition screening, management of waterborne and communicable diseases, trauma and emergency care, and specialized services such as gender-based violence (GBV) response and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS). Patient pathways within supported facilities will be reorganized to systematically identify and respond to the needs of vulnerable populations, including women, children under five, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities.ltbrgtTargeted service outputs include 24,563 outpatient consultations, 2,500 cases treated in Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) centers for acute watery diarrhea, and 3,500 children and 700 women vaccinated through routine immunization services. Antenatal care will be provided to at least 2,800 pregnant women, with 660 safe deliveries conducted under skilled attendance. Postnatal care will reach 1,000 lactating women within 6 weeks postpartum. Post-rape care services, in accordance with WHO’s clinical management of rape guidelines, will be offered to at least 100 survivors, alongside referral to protection partners and MHPSS support. Outreach activities will extend service coverage to 6,289 people in hard-to-reach areas.ltbrgtSpecial attention will be placed on strengthening infection prevention and control (IPC) at both community and facility levels. This includes the provision of IPC supplies, capacity building of healthcare workers, and community-based health promotion through trained integrated community health volunteers. Social mobilization campaigns will be conducted regularly to raise awareness of hygiene practices, disease prevention, maternal health, and available referral services.ltbrgtThe project ensures inclusion and equity by systematically collecting sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated data at all stages of the project. Specific interventions will target people with disabilities, with support from Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) to improve accessibility of services and infrastructure. Health services will be tailored to the unique needs of women and girls, including the provision of menstrual hygiene materials and secure, private spaces for service delivery.ltbrgtCoordination with existing CERF/CBPF and UNICEF-funded interventions particularly those implemented by DMO in Dinsor will ensure complementarity, prevent duplication, and enable knowledge sharing. DMO will engage with health and protection clusters, local authorities, and implementing partners through regular coordination meetings to streamline activities, harmonize referral mechanisms, and ensure alignment with national health strategies and humanitarian response plans.ltbrgtlt/pgt
